issues.title: Unsigned cross term discarded in the stability proof
issues.failure_explanation: The construction only proves a^K(Π_k^∇ṽ,d_h)=0, leaving a^K(Q_k^∇ṽ,d_h) with unrestricted sign. If that cross term is negative, subtracting it increases the expression, so the displayed final inequality does not follow.
issues.overall_effect: The upper equivalence for a_h^K is not proved, which removes the stated continuity bound used throughout the discrete stability and error analysis.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the sign-based final step in the upper-bound proof. The stabilization bounds and projector stability give a_h^K(v_h,v_h) ≤ C(|ṽ_h|_{1,K}²+|d_h|_{1,K}²), and the already-proved stable splitting bounds this by C|ṽ_h+d_h|_{1,K}². Summing over the elements and using symmetry recovers global continuity, leaving all dependent stability and error statements unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The discarded unsigned term is a genuine invalid inference, so this is not a typo. Nevertheless, a short local argument using estimates already proved in the old source restores the same equivalence and the entire affected chain without a new lemma, changed method, weakened guarantee, or rate loss.

issues.title: False full-norm coercivity claim for the pressure stabilization
issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that c_h controls ||q_h||_0 for every q_h∈Q_k. The definition and eq:stab_sp establish control only of ||Q_k^0q_h||_0. The difference is material because any nonzero mean-zero polynomial q_h has Q_k^0q_h=0 and c_h(q_h,q_h)=0 while ||q_h||_0>0.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed characterization of c_h is false, although the later weak inf-sup calculation uses the projected component and therefore does not require the false stronger bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace both full norms in the displayed characterization by the projected norm: δ_*‖Q_k^0q_h‖_{0,Ω}² ≤ c_h(q_h,q_h) ≤ δ^*‖Q_k^0q_h‖_{0,Ω}². No later argument needs alteration.
issues.why_classification: The definition c_h(p_h,q_h)=Σ_K S_p^K(Q_k^0p_h,Q_k^0q_h) and the immediately preceding kernel estimate uniquely force this correction. The surrounding text identifies c_h as stabilization of the nonpolynomial component, and subsequent reasoning already uses that component, so the omitted projectors are transcriptional and no mathematical inference or intended guarantee is repaired.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Construct and prove an H¹-stable, moment-preserving Clément-type quasi-interpolant J_h:H_0^1(Ω)→W̃_k with zero boundary trace, local estimate ‖v−J_hv‖_{0,K}+h_K|v−J_hv|_{1,K} ≤ Ch_K|v|_{1,ω_K}, and (v−J_hv,r)_K=0 for every r∈P_{k−2}(K). issues.why_classification: An H¹ input cannot be repaired by a notation change or by the old nodal interpolation proposition. Establishing a moment-preserving low-regularity quasi-interpolant is a contained but nontrivial new approximation lemma and construction. It does not require global proof reconstruction and preserves the full stability, well-posedness, and error-estimate chain, so the issue is moderate rather than serious.

issues.title: Uncontrolled bubble witness in the weak inf-sup construction

failure_location.quote: there exists $\bollatest_h\in\bubbleS$ such that the following equality holds

issues.failure_explanation: The scalar integral equality used in v1 does not by itself control the selected bubble's H^1 norm. The proof then passes to a velocity assembled from the interpolant and bubble without establishing the bounded-norm property needed to normalize it while retaining an h-uniform lower bound.
issues.overall_effect: The weak inf-sup witness is not shown to have a uniformly bounded discrete H^1 norm, so the stated normalization and the downstream stability chain are unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For each element, let e_K=v(q_h)−v_I and choose the unique d_K in the existing bubble space whose free moments agree with those of e_K for every vector polynomial in P_k(K)\P_{k−2}(K). The low moments already vanish, so this gives the required identity against ∇Π_k^0q_h. Using a^K(d_K,Π_{k+2}^∇d_K)=−(d_K,ΔΠ_{k+2}^∇d_K), moment matching, the polynomial inverse estimate, and the stated bubble projection bound yields |d_K|_{1,K} ≤ Ch_K^{-1}‖e_K‖_{0,K}. Summation gives a uniformly bounded witness v_I+d_h; a standard case split and rescaling supplies the stated normalization. The weak inf-sup and downstream chain then hold unchanged, without redefining the discrete spaces.
issues.why_classification: The scalar equality must be replaced by a uniformly bounded bubble lifting, and its h-independent norm estimate must be proved; this is more than a routine sign or bookkeeping correction. The required construction is nevertheless local and finite-dimensional and preserves the original method and every affected guarantee, so it is a contained moderate repair rather than a serious reconstruction.

issues.title: Missing positivity hypothesis for the pressure stabilization parameter

failure_location.quote: For any $(\u_h,p_h)\in\VV_k$ there exists a positive constant $\omega$ independent of $h$ such that

issues.failure_explanation: For a nonzero p_h∈Q_k∩ker(Π_k^0), b_h(v_h,p_h)=b(v_h,Π_k^0p_h)=0 for every v_h. At α=0, B_h[(0,p_h),(v_h,q_h)]=0 for every test pair, while ||p_h||_0>0. Such modes exist, for example, in the enhanced k=1 space on a single admissible quadrilateral. Thus the unconditional stability statement includes a false endpoint; the argument can support the result only for a fixed positive α.
issues.overall_effect: At α=0 the discrete bilinear form can have a nontrivial pressure kernel, so discrete stability, uniqueness, and the error analysis are not valid as unqualified claims.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Declare when defining the discrete problem that α is fixed, positive, and independent of h, and carry that qualification through the stability, uniqueness, and error results. In the standard B_h stability argument, choose the weak-inf-sup test multiplier small enough that its c_h contribution is dominated by αc_h; the constants may depend on the fixed α but remain independent of h.
issues.why_classification: The missing premise is substantive and therefore not a typo, since α=0 genuinely admits uncontrolled pressure modes. Positivity is, however, a short and standard qualification of the stabilization parameter, supported by the formulation and numerical regime; it preserves the method, conclusions, convergence rates, and intended positive-parameter regime with no nontrivial new argument.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof claims O(h) interpolation estimates for ψ∈H^2 and ρ∈H^1. In v1, the enhanced nodal estimate is stated only for H^{k+1} inputs, so it does not cover ψ when k>1; more decisively, an H^1 pressure need not have the nodal values needed to define ρ_I at all.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the enhanced nodal interpolation estimate for every regularity 2≤s≤k+1 and use its s=2 case for ψ. Replace the undefined nodal pressure interpolant by an H¹-defined Clément-type quasi-interpolant J_hρ∈Q_k satisfying ‖ρ−J_hρ‖_{0,Ω} ≤ Ch|ρ|_{1,Ω}; subtract its global mean if necessary to enforce membership in L_0². These choices establish the two O(h) dual interpolation bounds, after which the existing duality estimates recover the advertised h^{k+1} velocity L² rate.
issues.why_classification: The old source supplies neither the lower-regularity velocity estimate for k>1 nor any pressure interpolant defined on H¹. Supplying the required low-regularity quasi-interpolation result is a contained but nontrivial approximation construction, not a mere notation edit. It restores the same duality theorem and rate without global reconstruction or mathematical loss, so the issue is moderate.
